profile: SQLite 3.47.2 under the target, input and conflict conditions in sqlite-insert-input-v2.json and the result-slot conditions in sqlite-delete-returning-v1.json.
scope: Bind the supplied and returned positions of an ordinary INSERT to one absolute target. RETURNING observes the directly inserted new row.
structure: An absolute table and its immutable local slot layout.
An ordered list of supplied column references and an independent input role.
An optional ordered list of result names and referenced slots of the same table.
admission: Every supplied slot must be local to the target and distinct. A VALUES or SELECT input supplies one operand per ordered write slot. A default-only input supplies no write slots regardless of returned columns.
Analysis resolves supplied names and allocates implicit writable fields in declaration order. Generated fields are excluded from writes and can be returned.
Analysis resolves unqualified named fields and the unqualified wildcard. The ordered returned fields refer to existing target slots. The output width is at most 2000.
observations: Assigned values, defaults, INTEGER affinity, generated values and duplicate policy.

The exact names and typed row bag from RETURNING, including repeated fields and duplicate rows. A return row is produced for every directly inserted row before AFTER triggers change any of its fields.
The separate AFTER trigger state, affected row count, rollback, parameter slots and registered names.
A return slot can read a column omitted from the write input. Default-only inputs can return every target column with an empty write list.
sql: Render the absolute target and the supplied columns from their ordered slots. Emit the input first. Append unqualified quoted returned columns and labels after the input.

finite.identity: Recover the 72 tuples from the constructed operands and layout.

exploration.structure: Vary the input role, row count and operand trees, implicit/default-only or explicitly ordered write slots, filter and bindings, and returned widths, slots and labels.

open: Other conflict policies, qualified and general result expressions, virtual targets, WITH, UPSERT and additional source roles.
trust: Independent source, write and observer rules for the named fixture
Pinned SQLite and checked typed transport
External table identity and an AFTER trigger that changes stored rows
